text:
Situation: Calcium chloride injection is not on FDA's drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, lists its calcium chloride injection as To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2025-11-07. Corvale East holds 459 syringes (29.4 days on hand at 15.6 per day). Corvale General holds 245 syringes (16.2 days on hand at 15.1 per day).

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list does not include calcium chloride as of 2026-10-21. Hospira's product entry shows status To Be Discontinued since 2025-11-07. The Hospira label for NDC 00409163110 identifies a registered plant at FEI 1021343. That plant received a last inspection classification of NAI on 2025-02-07. The same plant received multiple OAI classifications in 2010 and 2011 and a Warning Letter on 2010-04-12.

Our position: Current inventory covers approximately 16 to 29 days depending on site. The sole manufacturer discontinuing is Hospira. Five alternative suppliers are not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase from ICU Medical Inc. (ranked option 1); requires buyer approval.
2. Buyer qualifies American Regent, Inc. as secondary source (ranked option 2); requires buyer approval.
3. Buyer qualifies Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC as tertiary source (ranked option 3); requires buyer approval.
4. Buyer qualifies B. Braun Medical Inc. as quaternary source (ranked option 4); requires buyer approval.
5. Buyer qualifies Becton Dickinson and Company as quinary source (ranked option 5); requires buyer approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or protocol revisions at this time; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
